# dsh-archived-sessions
English | 中文
A DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`) web plugin that adds an **Archived Sessions** section to the Settings pag
e for managing archived conversations.
> **Official source:** this repository is the official source of the npm package `dsh-archived-sessi
ons` — `dsh plugin add dsh-archived-sessions` installs exactly this code.
## Features
- **List archived sessions** — each row shows the session's own name (the same title the sidebar use

s), working directory, log size, and last update time.
- **Unarchive** — restore a session to the si

debar with one click; its original position in the workspace is kept.
- **Permanently delete** — rem
oves the session's local log directory (`~/.dsh/sessions/...`) plus the attachment objects its log r
eferences that no other remaining session still uses, then drops the session from workspace accounti

ng. A confirmation dialog must be acknowledged first.
- **Native look & feel** — built on the same U
I primitives and design tokens as the built-in Settings sections.
## Requirements
- DeepSeek Harness **0.2.0-rc.2 or newer** — the plugin consumes the `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-store`
snapshot store and the `remote.session` / `workspaces` client services, which replaced the former `

dsh-client-runtime` / `connection.api` surfaces.
- A core with the workspace **archive** surface (`w

orkspaceRegistry.archivedSessionIds` / `unarchiveSession`).
- Deletion needs **no extra core support
**. It clears the archive set through the existing `unarchiveSession`, whose contract is exactly wha
t a delete needs: it drops the id from `archivedSessionIds`, touches no accounting slot, runs no ses
sion-existence check, and no-ops on an id that is not archived. Workspace `sessionIds` need no write
either — that getter is already filtered by the canonical-cwd header index, so removing the log dro

ps the session from the workspace projection by itself.
- A core older than the archive surface stil
l degrades gracefully instead of failing: listing works, and the missing capability is reported as a
structured `partial` result rather than thrown.

## Usage

1. Archive a session from the sidebar session menu (it hides from the sidebar).
2. Open **Settings →

Archived Sessions**:
- **Unarchive** — restores the session to its original sidebar position.
- **D
elete** — opens a confirmation dialog; confirming permanently deletes the local log and related atta
chments (objects still referenced by other sessions are kept) and removes the session from workspace
ects still referenced by other sessions are kept) and removes the session from workspace accounting.
## Architecture
- **Host half** (`src/index.ts`) — registers `GET/POST /__dsh-archived-sessions/{list,unarchive,dele
te}` on the shared web server. The delete flow: dispose the live session first if it is open (so the
in-memory store drops it and persistence retires its state) → wait for the write-behind flush to ma
terialize the log → remove the session log directory → parse attachment references (`sha256:`) from
the log → delete only the objects no other remaining session references → clear the archive set via

`workspaceRegistry.unarchiveSession`.
- **Client half** (`src/client/`) — registers the `settings.se
ction` entry "Archived Sessions"; the list merges the `remote.session` listing (including the projec
tion title) with the plugin's host surface (creation time, log size); both mutations go through the
host surface because the core RPC map offers neither operation. After a successful delete the client
re-pulls the session-list baseline: deleting a cold (persisted, not-open) session emits no `session
/disposed`, so the sidebar would otherwise keep the stale row under **Ungrouped** until the next rec
ed`, so the sidebar would otherwise keep the stale row under **Ungrouped** until the next reconnect.
## Verification
There is no test runner in this repo; both checks are standalone Node scripts over the **built** art
ifacts, so run `pnpm run build` first.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
- `verify:delete` — points `DSH_HOME` at a throwaway tree and drives `lib/index.js` over a real HTTP
socket: list reports rows with log facts; delete removes the log directory, GCs only the attachment
objects no surviving session references (a shared object must survive), clears the archive set, and
reports a complete result; a core lacking `unarchiveSession` degrades to `partial` instead of throw

ing.
- `verify:client` — executes `lib/client.js` against stubs for the shell's frozen module table,
then mounts and renders the section. This catches the failure mode that once shipped a blank settin
gs page: a named import the shell does not export (e.g. the removed `IconTrashOutline16`) resolves t
o `undefined` and only throws at **render** time, inside the slot's error boundary, so the page rend
ers empty instead of failing loudly. Every name the bundle imports must be a real export of the shel
ad of failing loudly. Every name the bundle imports must be a real export of the shell's primitives.
